source.text: נִבְחָ֣ר שֵׁ֭ם מֵעֹ֣שֶׁר רָ֑ב מִכֶּ֥סֶף וּ֝מִזָּהָ֗ב חֵ֣ן טֽוֹב׃

records.literal_gloss: [Is] to be chosen a name more than riches great; more than silver and more than gold favor [is] good.

en.L: A [good] name [is] to be chosen rather than great riches; \q favor [is] better than silver and than gold.
en.B: A good reputation is worth choosing over great wealth; \q being well regarded is better than silver and gold.
en.R: Being known as a good person is worth more than being very rich. \q Being respected is better than having silver and gold.

decisions.choice: a name: a good reputation
decisions.reason: The bare word "name" here means a good name, the honor in which a person is held (Ecclesiastes 7:1).

decisions.choice: favor: the goodwill of others
decisions.reason: Favor (hen) is the kindness and respect others show a person (3:4; 13:15). With "more than", good means better.

decisions.choice: [good] name
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the word the Hebrew implies, in brackets.

source.text: עָשִׁ֣יר וָרָ֣שׁ נִפְגָּ֑שׁוּ עֹשֵׂ֖ה כֻלָּ֣ם יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Rich and poor meet together; [the] maker of all of them [is] YHWH.

en.L: [The] rich and [the] poor meet together; \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is the] Maker of them all.
en.B: Rich and poor alike share one thing: \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is the maker of them all.
en.R: Rich people and poor people are alike in one way. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} made every one of them.

decisions.choice: meet together: have this in common
decisions.reason: The rich and the poor cross paths in life, and what they share is that the LORD made both (14:31; 17:5; 29:13; Job 31:15).

decisions.choice: have this in common / are alike in one way
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state what the meeting means, so the line does not sound like a chance encounter.

source.text: עָר֤וּם׀רָאָ֣ה רָעָ֣ה וְנִסְתָּ֑ר וּ֝פְתָיִ֗ים עָבְר֥וּ וְֽנֶעֱנָֽשׁוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: A sensible [person] sees evil and hides himself, and naive [people] pass on and are punished.

en.L: A sensible [person] sees trouble and hides {{gender:themselves|himself}}, \q but [the] simple pass on and pay the penalty.
en.B: Sensible people see danger coming and take cover, \q but the naive walk straight into it and suffer for it.
en.R: Wise people see danger ahead and get out of the way. \q But people who do not think ahead keep going and get hurt.

decisions.choice: and hides himself, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The reading the scribes marked adds "and" to the verb; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: almost the same as 27:12
decisions.reason: 27:12 repeats this saying with small differences in the joining words.

decisions.choice: people who do not think ahead
decisions.reason: Readable describes the simple (petayim) instead of naming them.

source.text: עֵ֣קֶב עֲ֭נָוָה יִרְאַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה עֹ֖שֶׁר וְכָב֣וֹד וְחַיִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] reward of humility, [the] fear of YHWH, [is] riches and honor and life.

en.L: [The] reward of humility [and] the fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} \q [is] riches and honor and life.
en.B: Humility and the fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bring their reward: \q riches, honor, and life.
en.R: Be humble and honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with awe. \q Then you will receive riches, honor, and life.

decisions.choice: humility and the fear of the LORD: two linked virtues
alternatives: the reward of humility is the fear of the LORD, with riches, honor and life
decisions.reason: The two phrases stand side by side with no "and". They may be a pair (15:33 joins them), or the fear of the LORD may itself be the first reward of humility.

decisions.choice: reward: the result that follows
decisions.reason: The word (eqev) means what comes at the heel of something, its outcome (Psalm 19:12).

source.text: צִנִּ֣ים פַּ֭חִים בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ עִקֵּ֑שׁ שׁוֹמֵ֥ר נַ֝פְשׁ֗וֹ יִרְחַ֥ק מֵהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Thorns, snares [are] in [the] way of [the] crooked; [one who] guards his soul will be far from them.

en.L: Thorns [and] snares [are] in [the] path of [the] crooked; \q whoever guards {{gender:their|his}} life will keep far from them.
en.B: Thorns and traps lie on the road of the crooked; \q whoever values their life stays well away from them.
en.R: Dishonest people walk a path full of thorns and traps. \q If you want to protect your life, stay away from that path.

decisions.choice: thorns and snares: the troubles of a crooked life
decisions.reason: The crooked person's road is painful and dangerous (15:19). Whoever guards their life keeps off it (16:17; 19:16).

source.text: חֲנֹ֣ךְ לַ֭נַּעַר עַל־פִּ֣י דַרְכּ֑וֹ גַּ֥ם כִּֽי־יַ֝זְקִ֗ין לֹֽא־יָס֥וּר מִמֶּֽנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: Train the youth according to [the] mouth of his way; even when he grows old he will not turn from it.

en.L: Train a child according to {{gender:their|his}} way; \q even when {{gender:they grow|he grows}} old, {{gender:they|he}} will not turn from it.
en.B: Start children off on the way they should go, \q and even when they are old they will not leave it.
en.R: Teach children the right way to live while they are young. \q When they grow old, they will still live that way.

decisions.choice: according to his way: the way he ought to go
alternatives: the way suited to the child's own nature and stage of life
the way the child wants to go, said as a warning: let a child have his own way and he will never leave it
decisions.reason: "According to the mouth of his way" means "in keeping with his way", but whose standard sets the way is not stated. Proverbs speaks of one right way of wisdom (4:11), so the way he should go is taken here; the phrase can also mean training fitted to the child, or, less likely, a warning against leaving a child to himself (29:15).

decisions.choice: train: start off, dedicate
decisions.reason: The verb (hanak) is used of dedicating a house or the temple (Deuteronomy 20:5; 1 Kings 8:63): to begin something in the direction it is meant to go.

decisions.choice: child: a youth, boy or girl, from infancy to young adulthood
decisions.reason: The word (naar) covers a baby (1 Samuel 4:21) up to a young man (Genesis 37:2). The saying applies to any child; like other proverbs it states what usually happens rather than a promise.

decisions.choice: their / his
decisions.reason: The Hebrew pronoun is masculine but the saying is about any child, so Literal offers the inclusive and traditional pronoun as a setting.

source.text: עָ֭שִׁיר בְּרָשִׁ֣ים יִמְשׁ֑וֹל וְעֶ֥בֶד לֹ֝וֶ֗ה לְאִ֣ישׁ מַלְוֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: A rich [one] over [the] poor rules, and a servant [is the] borrower to [the] man [who] lends.

en.L: [The] rich rule over [the] poor, \q and [the] borrower [is] a slave to [the] one who lends.
en.B: The rich lord it over the poor, \q and whoever borrows becomes the lender's slave.
en.R: Rich people have power over poor people. \q If you borrow money, you come under the control of the one who lent it.

decisions.choice: the borrower is a slave: debt could end in servitude
decisions.reason: A debtor who could not pay might be sold, or have his children sold, to work off the debt (2 Kings 4:1; Nehemiah 5:5; Amos 2:6).

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" in Literal and Balanced, as the style guide keeps it where people are sold or held for debt: the word (eved) here describes a debtor's real loss of freedom (m1).

source.text: זוֹרֵ֣עַ עַ֭וְלָה יִקְצָר־אָ֑וֶן וְשֵׁ֖בֶט עֶבְרָת֣וֹ יִכְלֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: [One who] sows injustice will reap trouble, and the rod of his fury will come to an end.

en.L: Whoever sows injustice will reap trouble, \q and the rod of {{gender:their|his}} fury will come to an end.
en.B: Those who sow injustice will reap disaster, \q and the rod they swing in anger will fail.
en.R: People who do wrong will get trouble back, the way a farmer gets back the crop that was planted. \q The power they used in anger will be taken away.

decisions.choice: will reap, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: the rod of his fury will fail: his power to oppress will end
alternatives: the rod of God's fury will finish him
decisions.reason: The rod is the oppressor's means of beating others. The verb (kalah) can mean "come to an end" or "bring to an end", so the line may also say that his punishment will destroy him.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew ends the saying here
alternatives: the Greek translation adds: God blesses a cheerful and generous man
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation (the Septuagint) adds a line after this verse, which Paul echoes in 2 Corinthians 9:7. It is not in the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: the way a farmer gets back the crop that was planted
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the picture of sowing and reaping.

source.text: טֽוֹב־עַ֭יִן ה֣וּא יְבֹרָ֑ךְ כִּֽי־נָתַ֖ן מִלַּחְמ֣וֹ לַדָּֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: [One] good of eye, he will be blessed, for he gives from his bread to the poor.

en.L: [One with a] good eye will be blessed, \q for {{gender:they give|he gives}} from {{gender:their|his}} bread to the poor.
en.B: Generous people will be blessed, \q because they share their food with the poor.
en.R: People who give freely will be blessed. \q They share their food with poor people.

decisions.choice: good of eye: generous
decisions.reason: The "good eye" looks kindly on others and gives; the "evil eye" is stingy (23:6; 28:22).

decisions.choice: will be blessed: by God
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the one who blesses unnamed; the generous are rewarded as in 11:25 and 19:17.

source.text: גָּ֣רֵֽשׁ לֵ֭ץ וְיֵצֵ֣א מָד֑וֹן וְ֝יִשְׁבֹּ֗ת דִּ֣ין וְקָלֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: Drive out a mocker, and strife will go out, and dispute and insult will cease.

en.L: Drive out [the] mocker, and strife will go out; \q quarreling and insult will cease.
en.B: Throw out the mocker, and conflict goes too; \q quarrels and insults come to an end.
en.R: Send away the mocker, and the fighting will leave too. \q The arguing and the insults will stop.

decisions.choice: mocker: one who scorns correction and others
decisions.reason: The mocker (lets) sneers at wisdom and stirs up trouble (21:24; 26:20).

decisions.choice: dispute and insult: quarrels and the shame they bring
decisions.reason: The word for dispute (din) can mean a court case. Insult (qalon) is the dishonor heaped on people in a quarrel.

source.text: אֹהֵ֥ב טְהָר־לֵ֑ב חֵ֥ן שְׂ֝פָתָ֗יו רֵעֵ֥הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: [One who] loves purity of heart, grace [is in] his lips, his friend [is] a king.

en.L: Whoever loves purity of heart \q [and has] grace on {{gender:their|his}} lips, the king [is] {{gender:their|his}} friend.
en.B: Whoever loves a pure heart \q and speaks with grace will have the king for a friend.
en.R: Love what is pure, and speak kindly. \q Then even the king will want to be your friend.

decisions.choice: pure, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: the king befriends the pure in heart who speak graciously
alternatives: the king loves the pure in heart; one gracious in speech has him as friend
decisions.reason: The words are loosely joined, and the line can be divided in more than one way. The sense is that integrity and gracious speech win a ruler's favor (16:13). The Greek translation has the LORD, not a king, loving pure hearts.

source.text: עֵינֵ֣י יְ֭הוָה נָ֣צְרוּ דָ֑עַת וַ֝יְסַלֵּ֗ף דִּבְרֵ֥י בֹגֵֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: The eyes of YHWH guard knowledge, and he overturns [the] words of [one who] acts treacherously.

en.L: The eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} guard knowledge, \q but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} overturns [the] words of [the] treacherous.
en.B: The eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} keep watch over knowledge, \q but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brings the words of the faithless to nothing.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} watches over what is true. \q But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} ruins the plans of people who lie.

decisions.choice: knowledge: true knowledge and those who hold it
decisions.reason: The LORD protects what is true and the one who speaks it, in contrast to the treacherous in the second line.

decisions.choice: overturns: subverts, frustrates
decisions.reason: The verb (sillef) is used of the LORD overthrowing the wicked (13:6; 21:12) and of folly twisting a life (19:3).

source.text: אָמַ֣ר עָ֭צֵל אֲרִ֣י בַח֑וּץ בְּת֥וֹךְ רְ֝חֹב֗וֹת אֵֽרָצֵֽחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: Says [the] sluggard, A lion [is] outside! In [the] middle of [the] streets I will be killed!

en.L: [The] sluggard says, "[There is] a lion outside! \q I will be killed in [the] middle of the streets!"
en.B: The lazy one says, "A lion is out there! \q I will be murdered in the open street!"
en.R: A lazy person says, "I cannot go out. There is a lion out there! \q It will kill me in the street!"

decisions.choice: a lion outside: an absurd excuse to stay home
decisions.reason: The lazy one invents a danger to avoid going out to work (26:13). The verb for being killed (ratsah) is the word usually used of murder, which adds to the comedy.

decisions.choice: I cannot go out
decisions.reason: Readable states the point of the excuse, as in 26:13.

source.text: שׁוּחָ֣ה עֲ֭מֻקָּה פִּ֣י זָר֑וֹת זְע֥וּם יְ֝הוָ֗ה יִפָּל־שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: A pit deep [is the] mouth of strange [women]; [one] cursed [by] YHWH will fall there.

en.L: [The] mouth of strange [women is] a deep pit; \q [one who is] cursed [by] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will fall into it.
en.B: The talk of forbidden women is a deep pit; \q anyone {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is angry with will fall into it.
en.R: The sweet words of an immoral woman are like a deep pit. \q People {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is angry with will fall into it.

decisions.choice: the mouth of strange women: the seductive talk of women outside one's marriage
decisions.reason: The strange woman (zarah) belongs to another man; her smooth speech draws men in (2:16; 5:3; 7:5, 21).

decisions.choice: cursed by the LORD: the one under his indignation
decisions.reason: The word (zaam) is anger expressed in judgment. Falling into the pit is itself the judgment on such a person (Ecclesiastes 7:26).

decisions.choice: will fall, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The sense is the same.

source.text: אִ֭וֶּלֶת קְשׁוּרָ֣ה בְלֶב־נָ֑עַר שֵׁ֥בֶט מ֝וּסָ֗ר יַרְחִיקֶ֥נָּה מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Folly [is] bound in [the] heart of a youth; [the] rod of discipline will make it far from him.

en.L: Folly [is] bound up in [the] heart of a child; \q [the] rod of discipline will drive it far from {{gender:them|him}}.
en.B: Foolishness is tied fast to a child's heart, \q but the rod of discipline will drive it far away.
en.R: Children are naturally foolish. \q Firm correction will drive that foolishness out of them.

decisions.choice: the rod: physical discipline
decisions.reason: The rod was the usual means of correcting a child in the ancient world (13:24; 23:13–14; 29:15). The point of the saying is that love corrects; the means belongs to its time and must be read in the light of all Scripture says about love and justice.

decisions.choice: folly bound in the heart: foolishness comes naturally to the young
decisions.reason: Folly (ivvelet) is tied to the young heart like a knot (compare 1:22). Correction loosens it.

decisions.choice: firm correction
decisions.reason: Readable gives the purpose of the rod in plain words; the footnote on the meaning decision explains the picture.

source.text: עֹ֣שֵֽׁק דָּ֭ל לְהַרְבּ֣וֹת ל֑וֹ נֹתֵ֥ן לְ֝עָשִׁ֗יר אַךְ־לְמַחְסֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: [One who] oppresses [the] poor to increase for himself, [one who] gives to a rich [one]—only to want.

en.L: Whoever oppresses [the] poor to gain more for {{gender:themselves|himself}}, \q [or] gives to [the] rich, [comes] only to want.
en.B: Whoever exploits the poor to get rich, \q or hands gifts to the rich, will only end up in need.
en.R: Some people cheat the poor to get rich. \q Others give gifts to rich people to win favor. \q Both will end up poor.

decisions.choice: both oppressing the poor and giving to the rich end in want
alternatives: one who oppresses the poor may gain, but one who gives to the rich ends in want
one who oppresses the poor to enrich himself will end up giving to the rich, and so in want
decisions.reason: The two phrases are set side by side with no joining word, and their relation is unclear. Read as a pair, both ways of seeking gain backfire (11:24; 28:8).

decisions.choice: to win favor
decisions.reason: Readable gives the likely reason for gifts to the rich (19:6).

source.text: הַ֥ט אָזְנְךָ֗ וּ֭שְׁמַע דִּבְרֵ֣י חֲכָמִ֑ים וְ֝לִבְּךָ֗ תָּשִׁ֥ית לְדַעְתִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Incline your ear and hear [the] words of [the] wise, and your heart set to my knowledge,

en.L: Incline your ear and hear [the] words of [the] wise, \q and set your heart on my knowledge,
en.B: Bend your ear and hear what the wise have said, \q and set your mind on the knowledge I give,
en.R: Listen carefully to what wise people say. \q Think hard about what I am teaching you.

decisions.choice: the words of the wise: a new collection, 22:17–24:22
decisions.reason: These words open a collection in which a teacher speaks to a pupil (22:17–21) and then gives short sets of advice. It has close parallels with the Egyptian Instruction of Amenemope, which also opens by asking the pupil to give his ears to the sayings; 24:23 calls what follows "these also of the wise" (compare 1:6).

decisions.choice: set your heart: pay attention with the mind
decisions.reason: The heart is the place of thought and will (2:2; 23:12). "My knowledge" is what the teacher passes on.

source.text: כִּֽי־נָ֭עִים כִּֽי־תִשְׁמְרֵ֣ם בְּבִטְנֶ֑ךָ יִכֹּ֥נוּ יַ֝חְדָּ֗ו עַל־שְׂפָתֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: for [it will be] pleasant if you keep them in your belly; they will be ready together on your lips.

en.L: for [it is] pleasant if you keep them within you, \q [and] they [are] ready together on your lips.
en.B: for it is good to keep them deep inside you, \q every one of them ready on your lips.
en.R: It is good to remember them. \q Then you will always be ready to say them.

decisions.choice: in your belly: deep within you
decisions.reason: The belly stands for the inner self (18:8; 20:27). The Instruction of Amenemope also tells the pupil to keep its words in the casket of the belly.

decisions.choice: ready together on your lips: all at hand to be spoken
decisions.reason: The sayings are to be stored inside and also ready for use when the time comes to speak (15:23).

source.text: לִהְי֣וֹת בַּ֭יהוָה מִבְטַחֶ֑ךָ הוֹדַעְתִּ֖יךָ הַיּ֣וֹם אַף־אָֽתָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: So that your trust may be in YHWH, I have made [them] known to you today, even you.

en.L: So that your trust may be in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q I have made [them] known to you today, even to you.
en.B: I am teaching you today, yes, you, \q so that you will put your trust in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: I am teaching you these things today so that you will trust {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Yes, I am teaching you.

decisions.choice: trust in the LORD: the goal of the whole collection
decisions.reason: Whatever this collection shares with other ancient wisdom, it places its teaching under trust in the LORD (3:5; 16:20).

decisions.choice: even you: the pupil singled out
decisions.reason: The added pronoun makes the address personal: this teaching is for you.

source.text: הֲלֹ֤א כָתַ֣בְתִּי לְ֭ךָ שָׁלִישִׁ֑ים בְּמ֖וֹעֵצֹ֣ת וָדָֽעַת׃

records.literal_gloss: Have I not written for you thirty [sayings] in counsels and knowledge,

en.L: Have I not written for you thirty [sayings] \q of counsel and knowledge,
en.B: Have I not written you thirty sayings \q full of counsel and knowledge,
en.R: I have written down thirty sayings for you. \q They are full of good advice and knowledge.

decisions.choice: thirty, reading the scribes' word with different vowels
alternatives: excellent things, or officers, as the scribes' reading is usually pointed
decisions.reason: The written form reads "formerly" (shilshom); the reading the scribes marked (shalishim) is pointed as "excellent things" or "officers", which fits poorly. With different vowels the same word gives "thirty". The Instruction of Amenemope is made up of thirty chapters and asks the pupil to look at its thirty, and the collection that follows (22:22–24:22) can be read as about thirty sayings.

decisions.choice: thirty [sayings]
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has only the number; Literal brackets the word it implies.

source.text: לְהוֹדִֽיעֲךָ֗ קֹ֭שְׁטְאִמְרֵ֣י אֱמֶ֑ת לְהָשִׁ֥יב אֲמָרִ֥ים אֱ֝מֶ֗ת לְשֹׁלְחֶֽיךָ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: to make you know [the] certainty of words of truth, to bring back words of truth to those who send you?

en.L: to make you know [the] certainty of true words, \q so as to bring back true words to those who send you?
en.B: to teach you what is right and reliable, \q so that you can bring back a true answer to those who send you?
en.R: They teach you what is true and right. \q Then you can give a true report to the people who send you.

decisions.choice: bring back words to those who send you: report faithfully as a messenger
decisions.reason: The pupil is trained for service as a messenger or official who must answer for his errand (25:13). The Instruction of Amenemope also states its purpose as teaching a man to return an answer to the one who sent him.

decisions.choice: certainty: what is true and reliable
decisions.reason: The rare word (qoshet) means truth or what is right (Psalm 60:6). With "words of truth" it stresses how dependable the teaching is.

source.text: אַֽל־תִּגְזָל־דָּ֭ל כִּ֣י דַל־ה֑וּא וְאַל־תְּדַכֵּ֖א עָנִ֣י בַשָּֽׁעַר׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not rob a poor [one] because poor [is] he, and do not crush an afflicted [one] at the gate,

en.L: Do not rob [the] poor because {{gender:they are|he is}} poor, \q and do not crush [the] afflicted at the gate,
en.B: Do not rob the poor just because they are poor, \q and do not crush the needy in court,
en.R: Do not take things from poor people just because they are weak. \q Do not treat needy people unfairly in court.

decisions.choice: the gate: the place of the town court
decisions.reason: Elders sat at the town gate to judge cases (Ruth 4:1–2; Amos 5:12, 15). There the poor could be crushed by legal means.

decisions.choice: do not rob the poor: the first piece of advice
decisions.reason: The Instruction of Amenemope begins its advice with the same warning against robbing the wretched. The codex begins a new paragraph here.

decisions.choice: because he is poor: because he cannot defend himself
decisions.reason: Their weakness makes them an easy target; verse 23 names who defends them.

decisions.choice: because they are weak
decisions.reason: Readable names what makes the poor easy to rob.

source.text: כִּֽי־יְ֭הוָה יָרִ֣יב רִיבָ֑ם וְקָבַ֖ע אֶת־קֹבְעֵיהֶ֣ם נָֽפֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: for YHWH will plead their case, and he will rob those who rob them [of] life.

en.L: for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will plead their case \q and will rob [of] life those who rob them.
en.B: for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will take up their cause \q and take the life of those who plunder them.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will stand up for them in court. \q He will take the lives of people who rob them.

decisions.choice: plead their case: act as their advocate
decisions.reason: The LORD takes up the cause of the poor as their defender at law (23:11; Psalm 140:13).

decisions.choice: rob of life: punish the robber in kind
decisions.reason: The rare verb (qava) means rob (Malachi 3:8). Those who rob the poor are themselves robbed, of life.

source.text: אַל־תִּ֭תְרַע אֶת־בַּ֣עַל אָ֑ף וְאֶת־אִ֥ישׁ חֵ֝מוֹת לֹ֣א תָבֽוֹא׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not associate with a master of anger, and with a man of rages do not go,

en.L: Do not make friends with a master of anger, \q and with a person of rages do not go,
en.B: Do not make friends with someone hot-tempered, \q and do not keep company with those quick to rage,
en.R: Do not become friends with someone who gets angry easily. \q Do not spend time with people who lose their temper.

decisions.choice: master of anger, man of rages: a hot-tempered person
decisions.reason: The phrases describe someone ruled by anger (15:18; 29:22).

decisions.choice: do not befriend the hothead: a teaching shared with Amenemope
decisions.reason: The Instruction of Amenemope also warns against befriending the heated man and visiting him.

source.text: פֶּן־תֶּאֱלַ֥ף אֹֽרְחֹתָ֑יו וְלָקַחְתָּ֖ מוֹקֵ֣שׁ לְנַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: lest you learn his ways and take a snare for your soul.

en.L: or you will learn {{gender:their|his}} ways \q and take a snare for yourself.
en.B: or you may learn their ways \q and set a trap for your own life.
en.R: You might become like them. \q Then you would be caught in a trap.

decisions.choice: his ways, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The written form is singular; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: take a snare for your soul: trap your own life
decisions.reason: Learning the angry person's habits ensnares the learner too (13:20; 29:6).

source.text: אַל־תְּהִ֥י בְתֹֽקְעֵי־כָ֑ף בַּ֝עֹרְבִ֗ים מַשָּׁאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not be among [those who] strike [the] palm, among [those who] stand surety for debts.

en.L: Do not be among those who strike hands, \q among those who stand surety for debts.
en.B: Do not be one of those who shake hands on a pledge \q and guarantee other people's loans.
en.R: Do not promise to pay someone else's debts.

decisions.choice: strike the palm, stand surety: guarantee another's loan
decisions.reason: Striking hands sealed a promise to pay if the borrower did not (6:1–5; 11:15; 17:18).

source.text: אִם־אֵֽין־לְךָ֥ לְשַׁלֵּ֑ם לָ֥מָּה יִקַּ֥ח מִ֝שְׁכָּבְךָ֗ מִתַּחְתֶּֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: If there is nothing for you to pay, why will [anyone] take your bed from under you?

en.L: If you have nothing with which to pay, \q why should [anyone] take your bed from under you?
en.B: If you cannot pay, \q why let them take even the bed you sleep on?
en.R: If you cannot pay, you could lose everything, even your bed.

decisions.choice: take your bed: the creditor seizes even basic goods
decisions.reason: A creditor could take a debtor's goods as payment, though the law limited what could be taken from the poor (20:16; Exodus 22:26–27; Deuteronomy 24:12–13).

decisions.choice: statement instead of question
decisions.reason: Readable turns the warning question into a plain statement.

source.text: אַל־תַּ֭סֵּג גְּב֣וּל עוֹלָ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר עָשׂ֣וּ אֲבוֹתֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not move a boundary of antiquity that your fathers made.

en.L: Do not move [the] ancient boundary \q that your fathers set up.
en.B: Do not shift the old boundary stone \q that your ancestors put in place.
en.R: Do not move the old stones that mark where land ends. \q Your ancestors put them there.

decisions.choice: the ancient boundary: stones marking a family's land
decisions.reason: Fields were marked by boundary stones, and moving them was theft of inherited land (15:25; 23:10; Deuteronomy 19:14; 27:17). The Instruction of Amenemope also forbids moving boundary markers.

source.text: חָזִ֡יתָ אִ֤ישׁ׀מָ֘הִ֤יר בִּמְלַאכְתּ֗וֹ לִֽפְנֵֽי־מְלָכִ֥ים יִתְיַצָּ֑ב בַּל־יִ֝תְיַצֵּב לִפְנֵ֥י חֲשֻׁכִּֽים׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Do you see a man skilled in his work? Before kings he will stand; he will not stand before obscure [people].

en.L: Do you see a person skilled in {{gender:their|his}} work? \q {{gender:They|He}} will stand before kings; \q {{gender:they|he}} will not stand before obscure [people].
en.B: Do you see someone who is skilled at their work? \q They will serve kings, not people of no account.
en.R: Look at people who do their work with great skill. \q They will work for kings, not for unimportant people.

decisions.choice: stand before kings: serve in the royal court
decisions.reason: To stand before someone is to be in their service (1 Kings 10:8; 12:8).

decisions.choice: skilled: quick and expert
decisions.reason: The word (mahir) is used of a skilled scribe (Ezra 7:6; Psalm 45:2). The Instruction of Amenemope ends with the scribe skilled in his office who is found worthy to be a courtier.
